name: Badr al-Dīn Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Mālik
summary: Ibn Mālik's son, 'the son of the versifier', whose commentary on his father's Alfiyya was the first of the great ones and is still read, often to see where it corrects the poem.
bio: Badr al-Dīn grew up in Damascus with his father, Ibn Mālik, and learnt grammar from him; the sources say that for a time he lived apart from him in Baalbek, and that after his father's death in 672/1274 he took his place as teacher in Damascus. He died young, in 686/1287.

His Sharḥ Alfiyyat Ibn Mālik, called Sharḥ Ibn al-Nāẓim, explains the poem with care and does not hesitate to say where his father's verse is loose or his view weak; later commentators, Ibn Hishām and al-Ushmūnī among them, cite it constantly. He also wrote on rhetoric, an abridgement of al-Sakkākī's Miftāḥ called al-Miṣbāḥ.
